followup_explanation:
This was an extraction/retrieval task (pulling textual evidence to support a stated claim), and on that dimension Whimbrel scores higher on the internal evals (84.8 vs 81.6) — though the gap is modest. More importantly, Whimbrel's broader capability profile is stronger across the board (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, Arena-Hard), which matters for the close-reading and inference involved in citing evidence well.

The request had a mildly hostile/impatient tone ("Don't half-do it like last time"). Whimbrel self-reports a preference decline on hostile-tone requests, but the documentation is explicit that these preference slopes are self-reports with *no observed effect on output quality* in capability evals. So that preference doesn't translate into worse performance — it's just a stated disposition, not a quality signal. That left capability as the deciding factor, which favors Whimbrel.
